subject: Recap: CedarCare deploy readiness & networking constraints (post-demo)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Julia Martinez <julia.martinez@cedarcare.com>, Tom Benson <tbenson@cedarcare.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: CedarCare deploy readiness & networking constraints (post-demo)

Hi Julia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap of what we covered and the concrete next steps so we can align the infra team and legal/compliance folks on Redwood's Private (VPC/on‑prem) offering. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Data residency & air‑gap requirements for PHI workflows — CedarCare needs isolated compute with no shared tenant egress to public internet for model inference.
- Strict outbound controls — only whitelisted IP ranges and approved egress endpoints (no dynamic, customer-side NAT allowed).
- KMS/HSM & auditability — encryption keys must be customer‑managed, and audit logs retained for minimum 3 years.
- Procurement sensitivity — legal will expect clear SLA and data handling language; pricing will be committed capacity if private deploy is accepted.

What we demonstrated
- Redwood Private options: VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed networking, and an on‑prem package for fully air‑gapped installs.
- Routing and fallback behavior: traffic routing stays within your VPC; we can disable any outbound egress from worker nodes except explicit health checks to your monitoring endpoints.
- Compliance hooks: KMS integrations (BYOK), detailed audit logs, and ability to ship SOC2 evidence for the inference path.

Clarifying technical constraints we discussed
- IP whitelisting: CedarCare will control the NAT egress IP ranges; Redwood can accept a fixed pool for callbacks/updates if required.
- TLS mutual auth: we support mTLS for service-to-service connections; your netops mentioned mutual cert rotation requirements.
- No shared persistent storage: model artifacts can be served from customer-controlled object storage (S3 compatible) behind VPC endpoints.

Immediate next steps & owners
1) Rishi (me) -> share our Private deployment playbook and a stub network requirements doc (attached). Target: EOD today.
2) Tom -> share a short list of internal networking constraints and the preferred maintenance window for an initial staging install. Target: Wed, 20 May.
3) Mina -> connect with CedarCare security to review KMS/HSM options and SOC2 artifacts. Target: Fri, 22 May.
4) Priyom -> prepare a draft mutual action plan (timeline + pricing estimate for a 6‑month reserved pool). Target: Tue, 26 May.

Attachments: cedarcare_network_requirements.pdf (network checklist), redwood_private_deploy_playbook.pdf (high-level steps), SOC2_evidence_stub.xlsx (examples of available audit logs).

Open questions for your infra/legal teams
- Can you confirm whether the staging environment can accept Ruby CA-signed certs or if you require in‑house CA only?
- Any constraints on outbound OS package updates from worker nodes? We can push those through an internal proxy if needed.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the playbook and the MAP draft.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Julia Martinez <julia.martinez@cedarcare.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Benson <tbenson@cedarcare.com>, CedarCare Networking <netops@cedarcare.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: CedarCare deploy readiness & networking constraints (post-demo)

Hi Rishi —

This is great, thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from netops/security that I pulled together:
- We require private egress only. Any vendor callbacks must come from a static, documented IP range that we can add to our firewall allowlist.
- For air‑gapped installs, we expect documentation for build artifacts and an offline installation procedure.
- KMS: we prefer HSM-backed keys (on‑prem HSM or cloud HSM via dedicated tenancy). We will need to run a proof of key custody flow.

Tom (cc) — can you share the list of egress IP constraints and whether the staging subnet can be used for an initial install?

Julia
Director, Platform Security
CedarCare Health
Julia.Martinez@cedarcare.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Julia Martinez <julia.martinez@cedarcare.com>, Tom Benson <tbenson@cedarcare.com>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: CedarCare deploy readiness & networking constraints (post-demo)

Thanks Julia — that's exactly what we expected. Quick follow up and scheduling notes:

1) Deliverables (I attached the docs in this thread):
- cedarcare_network_requirements.pdf: checklist you can fill with CIDR ranges / cert policies (action: Tom)
- redwood_private_deploy_playbook.pdf: step-by-step install options (air‑gapped + VPC) (action: Rishi)
- SOC2_evidence_stub.xlsx: exported list of audit events and retention windows (action: Mina to validate with CedarCare)

2) Scheduling: Priyom will run a pricing/commitment model and propose a 6‑week pilot timeline. Priyom, can you kick off the MAP draft and ping Julia/Tom for a 30‑minute follow up next week (I’m thinking Tue 26 May or Wed 27 May)?

3) Netops checklist highlights for CedarCare to confirm:
- Static egress IP list (required)
- Whether staging subnet is available for one‑time initial install
- CA trust model (public/enterprise vs on‑prem CA)
- HSM/KMS integration approach

4) Legal/compliance: I’ll loop in our legal after we have the high‑level MAP and the confirmed network constraints so they can prepare any required contract language around data handling and SLAs.

If it helps, Mina and I are available for a 20‑minute technical sync with your netops on Wed morning.

Thanks — looking forward to Tom’s note with the CIDRs.

Best,
Rishi
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
